'''Chinese American Citizens Alliance''' ('''C.A.C.A.''') is a [[Chinese American]] [[Kongsi|fraternal, benevolent]] non-profit organization founded in 1895 in [[San Francisco, California]] to secure equal rights for Americans of Chinese ancestry and to better the welfare of their communities. C.A.C.A. is the [[United States]]' oldest [[History of Asian Americans|Asian American]] civil rights organization.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CREC-2012-06-18/html/CREC-2012-06-18-pt1-PgH3715-2.htm|title = Congressional Record Volume 158, Number 92 (Monday, June 18, 2012)|publisher = Government Publishing Office}}</ref>

== Organization ==
C.A.C.A. was originally named the ''Native Sons of the Golden State'' (similar to the [[Native Sons of the Golden West]]) and changed to its present name in 1915 to reflect its national presence.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=History |url=https://www.cacanational.org/about/history |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=www.cacanational.org |language=en-US}}</ref> By that time, three lodges within California in [[Los Angeles]] (1914), [[San Francisco]] (1915), and [[Oakland, California|Oakland]] (1917) were chartered as local lodges. In the early 1920s, the building housing the national headquarters at 1044 [[Stockton Street (San Francisco)|Stockton Street]] in [[San Francisco]] was completed.<ref name=":0" /> As interest for local lodges grew beyond the [[California|Golden State]], the organization's name was changed to accommodate a national alliance, the Chinese American Citizens Alliance.

As of 2026, there are twenty local lodges around the United States, including [[Albuquerque, New Mexico|Albuquerque]], [[Boston]], [[Houston, Texas|Houston]], [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]], [[Los Angeles, California|Los Angeles]], [[Greenville, Mississippi|Greenville]], [[Oakland, California|Oakland]], [[Orange County, California|Orange County]], Peninsula ([[Santa Clara County, California|Santa Clara]]), [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix]], [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], [[Salinas, California|Salinas]], [[San Antonio, Texas|San Antonio]], [[San Gabriel Valley|Greater San Gabriel Valley]], [[San Francisco, California|San Francisco]], [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]], [[Chicago, Illinois|Chicago]], [[Seattle]], [[Washington, D.C.]], and [[New York metropolitan area|Greater New York]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lodges |url=https://www.cacanational.org/get-involved/lodges |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=www.cacanational.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

The Board Officers are the governing body of the Alliance with its officers elected during each biennial convention. Local lodges each have their own lodge officers and associates. In addition, each local lodge annually chooses a National Representative to serve in a liaison capacity between their own lodge and the Board Officers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Board Officers |url=https://www.cacanational.org/about/board-officers |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=www.cacanational.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Mission and values ==
The Purposes and Objectives of the Chinese American Citizens Alliance are to empower Chinese Americans by:<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.cacanational.org/about |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=www.cacanational.org |language=en-US}}</ref>
*pursuing the highest ethics, morals, and values, practicing and defending American citizenship and American patriotism, 
* bettering the economic and political opportunities in our communities,
* preserving their historical and cultural traditions, and
* assuring the education of their youth and community.
The Principles each Member must abide by are:<ref name=":1" />
* "A Member shall be a person of highest character and shall uphold the principles of charity, justice, fidelity, fellowship, and mutual help of other Members, shall support the pursuit of knowledge, and must suppress self-interest to foster an organization united in cause for the good of community and our Alliance."

== History ==
C.A.C.A has had over a century of [[Civil and political rights|civil rights]] advocacy and local community development. ''The Chinese Times'', founded in 1924 by [[Walter U. Lum]], became the official and national newspaper of the Alliance for over 60 years and, at one point, grew to the largest circulated Chinese language newspaper in the country.<ref name=":0" /> Many community projects, such as the [[City College of San Francisco|City College of San Francisco Chinatown/North Beach campus]], San Francisco Chinatown Playground, and a San Francisco Chinatown police substation, have been due to the efforts and influence of Alliance members.

In recent times, C.A.C.A. continues to promote immigrant literacy programs, support the preservation of historical sites and landmarks, and approach local and state governments to ensure [[Asian American]] topics are adequately covered in school curriculums.<ref name=":0" /> In 2012, through the collective effort of many Asian Americans including members of the C.A.C.A., worked with the [[112th United States Congress|112th Congress]] to secure the passage of two resolutions (H Res. 683 and S. Res. 201), expressing regret for the passage of [[Chinese Exclusion Act|Chinese Exclusion Laws]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rep. Chu |first=Judy [D-CA-32 |date=2012-06-18 |title=Text - H.Res.683 - 112th Congress (2011-2012): Expressing the regret of the House of Representatives for the passage of laws that adversely affected the Chinese in the United States, including the Chinese Exclusion Act. |url=https://www.congress.gov/bill/112th-congress/house-resolution/683/text |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=www.congress.gov}}</ref> For H Res. 683, the House of Representatives passed the resolution by unanimous consent expressing regret over the [[Chinese Exclusion Act|Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-08 |title=Chinese Exclusion Act (1882) |url=https://www.archives.gov/milestone-documents/chinese-exclusion-act |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=National Archives |language=en}}</ref>

C.A.C.A. has had a history of youth outreach programs. The Chinese American Citizens Alliance LA Lodge Youth Council (YC) was formed in August 2001 and is supported by the Chinese American Citizens Alliance, Los Angeles Chapter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=jhomedia.com.tw |title=Chinese American Citizens Alliance Organization |url=http://en.ccbala.org/home/productdetail/115906 |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=en.ccbala.org |language=zh}}</ref> It was created in response to the growing number of students seeking college entry counseling. The main goals of the Youth Council are to assist students with the college admission process, provide opportunities for them to perform community service and for youth leadership development.  Membership currently consists of high school students, college students, and recent college graduates residing in the [[San Fernando Valley]], [[Chinatown, Los Angeles|Chinatown]],  Foothill ([[Arcadia, California|Arcadia]] and [[Temple City, California|Temple City]]), [[San Gabriel Valley|West and East San Gabriel Valley]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://cacayc-sfv.synthasite.com/about-us.php|title = Chinese American Citizens Alliance Youth Council}}</ref>

== Notable events ==
* '''1895''' – [[Chinese American]]s in San Francisco establish the ''Native Sons of the Golden State'' in response to racism and prejudice that limited their employment, education, housing, insurance and banking opportunities. Full citizenship and informed civic engagement are key tenets.<ref name=":0" />
* '''1912''' − The cities of [[San Francisco]], [[Los Angeles]], and [[Oakland, California|Oakland]] establish lodges.
* '''1915''' − A new national charter is adopted to form the Chinese American Citizens Alliance under a Grand Lodge based in [[San Francisco]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url = http://www.cacanational.org/CACA_pdf/CACA_National_Brochure_(Final).pdf|title = C.A.C.A. Brochure}}</ref>
* '''1921''' – C.A.C.A builds a National Headquarters in San Francisco.
* '''1924''' – C.A.C.A publishes ''Chinese Times'' as its official newspaper. It is the first Chinese language newspaper to be owned, edited, and published by American citizens. For 60 years, it was the principal source of national news and commentary for [[Chinese American]] communities.
* '''1943''' − Congress repeals [[Chinese Exclusion Act|Chinese exclusion]] provisions to permit Chinese to immigrate (albeit limited to 105 worldwide per year) and become American citizens. 
* '''1946''' – With C.A.C.A. backing, Congress removes immigration restrictions that prevented Chinese from benefiting from the [[War Brides Act|1945 War Brides Act]] as non-quota wives and children of American citizens.
* '''1965''' – [[Hart-Cellar Act]] removes race and national origins as basis for immigration. It comes on the heels of the [[Civil Rights Act of 1964]] and the [[Voting Rights Act of 1965]] to atone for past discrimination.
* '''2000''' – With C.A.C.A. support, California voters passed a state bond measure that set aside $15 million specifically for restoration of the [[Angel Island Immigration Station]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.aiisf.org/education/station-history/restoration|title = Angel Island Immigration Station Foundation|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150811042606/http://www.aiisf.org/education/station-history/restoration|archive-date = 2015-08-11|url-status = dead}}</ref>
* '''2008''' – C.A.C.A. wins House recognition of the contributions of Asian American/Pacific Islander soldiers who fought in the [[American Civil War]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.army.mil/asianpacificamericans/history|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140503014824/http://www.army.mil/asianpacificamericans/history|url-status = dead|archive-date = May 3, 2014|title = Asian Pacific Americans in the United States Army}}</ref>
* '''2012''' – C.A.C.A., with five national Asian American organizations, obtains Senate and House unanimous resolutions condemning the [[Chinese Exclusion Act|Chinese exclusion laws]] first enacted in 1882.
* '''2014''' – The [[United States Department of Labor|U.S. Department of Labor]], with C.A.C.A. assistance, inducts Chinese [[transcontinental railroad]] workers into its Wall of Honor.
* '''2018''' – C.A.C.A. establishes recognition for Chinese American World War II Veterans with a Congressional Gold Medal.<ref name=":0" />
* '''2022''' – Chinese American Citizens Alliance Albuquerque Lodge records available for research<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chinese American Citizens Alliance Albuquerque Lodge records available for research |url=https://news.unm.edu/news/chinese-american-citizens-alliance-albuquerque-lodge-records-available-for-research |access-date=2026-10-22 |website=UNM UCAM Newsroom |language=en}}</ref>
